claims.text: Premelting onset and progression in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are governed by Cu-rich surface segregations.
Cu-rich surface segregations lower the local melting barrier.
Controlled oxidative etching can remove or alter Cu-rich surface regions.
Removing or altering Cu-rich surface regions will delay premelting onset.
Removing or altering Cu-rich surface regions will narrow the phase-transition temperature range.
The as-synthesized FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are initially solid.
The as-synthesized untreated nanoparticles possess native Cu-rich surface segregations.
Cu-rich surface segregation alters nanoparticle surface energy.
Altered surface energy at Cu-rich regions locally lowers the melting temperature.
Cu-rich surface domains are energetically unstable.
Cu-rich surface domains act as initiation sites for premelting.
The locally reduced melting temperature produces higher atomic mobility at Cu-rich surface sites.
Selective etching of Cu-rich regions minimizes local surface-energy disparity.
Etched nanoparticles will have a higher apparent premelting-onset temperature than untreated nanoparticles.
Etched nanoparticles will exhibit a narrower melting range than untreated nanoparticles.
Etched nanoparticles will exhibit fewer disordered surface regions than untreated nanoparticles during heating.
Variation in heating rate can confound the observed thermal response.
Nonselective etching can confound the comparison between etched and untreated nanoparticles.

contradictions.description: The intervention permits selective removal of Cu-rich material, while the boundary condition requires that overall alloy composition not be altered. Actual removal of Cu can change composition unless the amount is explicitly shown to be negligible.

The boundary treats nonselective etching and secondary compositional changes as confounds, but the falsification rule treats extensive off-target compositional change as falsification. Such a result would normally invalidate the intervention rather than decisively falsify the proposed mechanism.
